name: Elim Beach
correct_wikipedia: none (no 'Elim Beach' or 'Elim, Queensland' article; Elim is covered in 'Hope Vale, Queensland')

facts.f: Elim Beach is home to the Coloured Sands, whose dune formations are a 300 m walk along the beach; campground at the water's edge with views to Cape Bedford
Drive from Hope Vale to Elim takes about an hour on a sealed road through white silica sand hills; 4WD only on the beach, at low tide, with extreme caution
Elim Aboriginal Mission was established in 1895 on the beach on Cape Bedford's north shore, later moved inland to Hope Vale
Coloured Sands permit about $10 from the Hope Vale service station (map included); permit price from a 3rd-party page, council page says 'Coloured Sands permit and camping' without price

cost.note: Aboriginal land permit; per person vs vehicle not stated: confirm with Hope Vale council. Camping fee separate.

name: Australian Age of Dinosaurs
correct_wikipedia: Australian Age of Dinosaurs (correct as is)
category_note: placement category 'beach' is wrong: use museum

facts.f: Nonprofit museum in Winton founded 2002 by David and Judy Elliott; holds the largest collection of Australian dinosaur fossils, including holotypes of Diamantinasaurus matildae, Savannasaurus elliottorum and Australovenator wintonensis; runs a fossil preparation laboratory
Site designated Australia's first International Dark-Sky Sanctuary in 2019
Outback Queensland lists indicative rates $78 to $260

name: Mount Morgan
correct_wikipedia: Mount Morgan, Queensland (town) or Mount Morgan Mine (the visitor attraction; article has coordinates -23.64111, 150.37528)
pin_flag: placement pin -23.633333,150.383333 is a rounded town-centre point, not a viewpoint or the mine; category 'viewpoint' is wrong. Re-pin on the mine/Arthur Timms Lookout (or make it a town spot) via resolve-pin.py.

facts.f: Mount Morgan is a rural town in the Rockhampton Region, former administrative centre of Mount Morgan Shire until 2008

The former mine (1882-1981; copper, gold, silver) is now a tourist attraction with remaining structures including the General Office, Gold Rooms and Main Stack; the Arthur Timms lookout overlooks the mine buildings and township
Wikivoyage suggests a railway tour at the former gold-mining town

name: Black Stump
correct_wikipedia: Blackall, Queensland (Black Stump is a general idiom article; the Blackall monument has no own article)

facts.f: Blackall claims the origin of 'beyond the black stump'; the stump marked the original Astro Station of 1887, was moved to Thistle Street for tourists, and the current one is a reconstruction after the original burned
Monument in Thistle Street has an explanation of the town's claim
